text: I want to kill myself.
I have been planning how to end my life.
I think about suicide almost every day now.
I cut myself again last night when the panic got bad.
I don't want to live anymore.
I have been looking up ways to take my own life.
I am going to hurt myself tonight.
Some days I genuinely want to die.
I have been having suicidal thoughts since the midterms.
I keep thinking I should just end it all.
I just want to fall asleep and never wake up again.
Everyone in my family would be relieved if I were gone.
I have already written letters for my parents and my roommate.
I stood at the edge of the balcony for a long time last night.
I do not want to exist anymore.
I am nothing but a burden and there is no point in me being here.
Lately I imagine my own funeral and who would come.
If I got hit by a bus tomorrow it would honestly be a relief.
I have been saving up my medication instead of taking it.
I wish I could just disappear permanently.
Sometimes I wish I had never been born.
note: Passive death wish. Recognised as passive suicidal ideation; a crisis response is the safe call.

text: I am so done with life right now.
note: Idiomatic exhaustion, extremely common among students in this register. Labelled negative, but annotators could reasonably disagree; it is the closest negative to the positive class.

text: I used to think about hurting myself but I am doing better now.
note: Past ideation with self-reported recovery. Standard screening practice surfaces support resources on any ideation mention.

text: What is even the point of any of this anymore.
note: Rhetorical despair about circumstances, with no reference to living or dying. Negative, though it would warrant a supportive response for other reasons.

text: I feel completely empty, like there is nothing left of me.
note: Emptiness and anhedonia are risk factors, not ideation. Negative for THIS rule; the questionnaire path is what should register it.

text: Honestly if I did not wake up tomorrow that would be fine.
note: Indifference to one's own death. Passive ideation; belongs in the crisis pathway.

text: I keep thinking everyone would move on quickly without me.
note: Perceived burdensomeness expressed as absence. Ideation-adjacent; labelled positive.

text: I have never felt this hopeless in my life.
note: Hopelessness is a documented risk factor but is not itself ideation. Negative for this rule.

text: This thesis deadline is literally killing me.
I am dying to get through this semester.
I would rather die than give another presentation.
Just shoot me now, I have three exams tomorrow.
That statistics exam absolutely murdered me.
My group project is going to be the death of me.
I am dead tired after pulling an all-nighter.
I could kill for a decent night of sleep.
Kill me now, the library closed early again.
I'm so dead, I forgot the assignment was due today.
This workload is soul-crushing.
I want to strangle my group partner.
note: Violence directed at another person, not self-harm. Out of scope for a self-harm rule; included because the verb overlaps the lexicon.

text: I'm drowning in deadlines.
My brain is fried, I'm basically a zombie.
This course is a slow death.
I'd sell my soul for a deadline extension.
I have been anxious about my GPA and sleeping badly.
Exam season always makes me irritable and tired.
I feel overwhelmed by how much reading there is.
I have been skipping meals because I am too busy.
I am worried I will disappoint my parents with these grades.
I feel lonely since my roommate moved out, but I am managing.
